mentor.name: Mémé Truelle
mentor.hello: Welcome to the site. I'm Mémé Truelle, forty years on building sites. We'll go one step at a time.
mentor.notYet: Not yet. I don't see it on GitHub. Did it go?
mentor.connectGithub: To do it for real, the site office needs your GitHub key: run gh auth login, then reload.
mentor.rankDone: That's the Apprentice rank. You know your way around now.

a1-walk.goal: Walk with the keys or the arrows, then open a pallet.
a1-walk.lesson: First, look around. Each crate on a pallet is a piece of work. Go and open one.
a1-walk.done: There. You can walk and look. That's half the job.

a2-read-issue.goal: Read the open card: its title, its text, its labels. Then press "Got it, Mémé".
a2-read-issue.lesson: That's an issue. A job written down so nobody forgets it. Read the title first, always.
a2-read-issue.done: Title, text, labels. You read it like a pro.

a3-read-board.goal: Push a pallet to another yard and confirm.
a3-read-board.lesson: Each fenced yard is a column of the board. When a pallet moves on, the work moves on. Push one, you'll see.
a3-read-board.done: See? The pallet moved, the work moved. That's all a board is.

a4-found-site.goal: Create your practice site: a repository and its board, in your own GitHub account.
a4-found-site.lesson: Enough of the pretend site. You get your own, in your own account. Nobody else's work is at risk there.
a4-found-site.done: Your own site. Your name on the gate.

a5-write-issue.goal: Write your first issue on your site: a clear title, a few words of text.
a5-write-issue.lesson: A good issue says what to do and why, with a title anyone understands. Short is fine.
a5-write-issue.done: Your first issue. Written down, nobody forgets it.

a6-take-issue.goal: Take your issue: assign yourself and say so in a comment.
a6-take-issue.lesson: When you take a job, say it out loud. Then everyone knows it's yours.
a6-take-issue.done: You said "I'll take it". Now everyone knows it's yours. Nobody else will do it twice.

a7-move-issue.goal: Push your issue out of the first column of your board.
a7-move-issue.lesson: Work you've started belongs in the next column. The board must say what's true.
a7-move-issue.done: Moving on. Your board tells the truth.
